claim: At grant, US8278036B2 lists inventors Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman, is assigned to the University of Pennsylvania / The Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania, and states the invention was supported in part by NIH grants with U.S. Government rights reserved.
metric_value: Penn assignee; NIH grants AI060505, AI50484, DE14825 stated
notes: Origin / ownership / government-rights facts from the patent document. Not a commercial value amount and not an exact product mapping.

claim: Karikó et al. (Immunity, 2005) report that RNA signaling through human TLR3/7/8 is reduced or abolished when nucleosides are modified (including m5C, m6A, m5U, s2U, or pseudouridine), lowering dendritic-cell activation relative to unmodified RNA.
metric_value: modified nucleosides suppress TLR-mediated RNA immunogenicity
notes: Peer-reviewed mechanism evidence supporting technical differentiation and early option/future-use potential. Not E3 product mapping and not patent-level attributable value.

claim: Karikó et al. (Molecular Therapy, 2008) report that pseudouridine-containing mRNA shows higher translational capacity and lower immunogenicity in vitro and in mice, and conclude that such modified mRNA is a promising tool for gene replacement and vaccination.
value_carrier: aspirational therapeutic / vaccine mRNA modality (not a marketed product at T0)
metric_value: explicit gene-replacement and vaccination framing with in-vivo nonimmunogenic translation evidence
notes: Package B option/future-value signal observable before commercial COVID vaccines. Must not be read as R3 implementation in a marketed product at T0=2012-10-02.

claim: The granted patent claims and describes RNA comprising pseudouridine or other modified nucleosides and methods spanning gene therapy / therapeutic protein delivery and reduced RNA immunogenicity, including illustrative disease/use embodiments (e.g., anemia/EPO, CFTR, ADA SCID).
value_carrier: claimed therapeutic RNA modality (patent text; no marketed carrier confirmed at T0)
metric_value: modified-nucleoside RNA for therapeutic protein expression / reduced immunogenicity
notes: Claimed/described future uses support option-horizon interpretation. They are not proof that any marketed vaccine or drug embodied this exact patent at T0.
